in_arabic.name: طاهب
in_arabic.meaning: الطيب والزكي والمطهر من كل سوء وشر
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم الطاهب مشتق من الجذر الطهارة، ويعني الشخص الذي يمتلك طبيعة طيبة وزكية، ومطهرة من كل سوء وشر، وقد وردت هذه المعاني في القرآن الكريم في عدة آيات، منها قوله تعالى: 'وَيُطَهِرُكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا'، وتستخدم هذه التسمية في الثقافة الإسلامية لتعبر عن الشخص الذي يتمتع بالطهارة الداخلية والخارجية.

in_urdu.name: طاہب
in_urdu.meaning: طیب و زکی اور ہر برائی سے پاک
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام طاہب عربی زبان کے جڑ الطہارة سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ایک ایسا شخص جس کی فطرت اچھی اور زکی ہے، اور ہر برائی اور شر سے پاک ہے۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں ان شخصیات کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اندرونی اور بیرونی طور پر پاکیزگی کے حامل ہوں۔

in_english.name: Tahib
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tahib originates from the Arabic root الطهارة (al-ṭahārah), meaning 'purification' or 'chastity'. It refers to someone with an inherently pure and clean nature, free from evil and impurities. This name is used in Islamic tradition to signify individuals who embody inner and outer purity, as mentioned in several Quranic verses, such as 'And He cleanses you thoroughly' (33:33). The name holds significant spiritual meaning, reflecting desirable personality traits like innocence, moral integrity, and cleanliness of heart and soul.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah'. In this seminal work of medieval Islam, Ibn Khaldun describes a dynasty known as the 'Hamdanids' who ruled in northern Syria and Iraq from the late 9th to the early 11th century CE. The Hamdanids' power base was at Mosul, where they established a center of Islamic learning and culture. One of their rulers, Badh al-Jamali (1075-1095 CE), is reported to have had a vizier named Tahib ibn Yazid. Tahib was a poet, scholar, and administrator who played an important role in the Hamdanid court.
historical_references.context: Hamdanid Dynasty, Mosul, Islamic learning and culture

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's 'The History of Damascus'. In this extensive historical work, al-Maqrizi describes a significant figure in the early Abbasid period named Tahib ibn Muadh. He was a prominent Damascene scholar and poet who lived during the caliphate of Harun al-Rashid (763-809 CE). Tahib was a patron of the sciences and the arts and is said to have founded a madrasa (school) in Damascus. He was also a prolific writer, composing texts on various subjects including biography, history, and poetry.
historical_references.context: Damascus, patron of sciences and arts, madrasa foundation
